annotations.annotation_text: HCE manifestation "Humphrey Chimpden" on page 30 within "The Encounter in Phoenix Park": here the universal father-figure Humphrey Chimpden Earwicker appears in the context of HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. During this Age of Gods phase, HCE embodies the patriarch whose guilt, grandeur, and fall drive the cyclical dream forward.
sources: Glasheen, Adaline. Third Census of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/thirdcensusoffin0000glas
McHugh, Roland. The Sigla of Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/siglaoffinnegans0000mchu
James Joyce Digital Archive: Finnegans Wake Notons. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "genesis" on page 30 ("The Encounter in Phoenix Park"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through HCE's mysterious sin in Phoenix Park, the spread of gossip through Dublin, and the Cad with the pipe. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Gods phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.
sources: Contemporary Literature Press: Classical Lexicon for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Frazer, Sir James George. Folk-Lore in the Old Testament. https://archive.org/details/folkloreinoldtes01frazuoft
